summary: Startup acquisitions can reshape employees’ finances and careers, with individual outcomes depending on a variety of conditions. Guest author Ron Honig, co-CEO and managing partner of From-Honig Family Office, suggests that before making major life changes, employees should clarify their award rights, when proceeds will become available, and what their after-tax payout can realistically support.
title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight

summary: Crunchbase News spoke with James Kim, partner at Reach Capital, about how Reach’s education roots inform its broader strategy, what it saw in AI detection company GPTZero, and why some of its best investments initially divided its own team. We also discussed how ownership stakes and secondary transactions have shaped the firm’s approach to returning capital.
title: ‘Weird And Maybe Uninvestable’: How Reach Capital Spots Its Venture Winners

summary: Founders can build billion-dollar businesses without venture capital by prioritizing customer revenue, pricing for quality, hiring exceptional talent and automating processes to scale efficiently, argues Nacho De Marco, who draws on his experience bootstrapping BairesDev, to emphasize financial discipline and a lasting commitment to solving customer problems as the foundations of sustainable growth.
title: How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital

summary: All told, fintech startups raised $10.6 billion globally in the third quarter of 2026, down 28.4% from $14.9 billion in Q2 2026 and 21.4% from $13.5 billion in Q3 2025.
title: Fintech Funding Fell 21% In Q3 As Deals Grew Scarcer

title: LatAm Startup Funding Jumps 26% In Q3 As VCs Begin ‘Rediscovering’ The Region

summary: Enterprise AI companies relying on armies of forward deployed engineers are disguising labor-intensive services as scalable software, inflating recurring revenue and valuations while falling short of autonomy claims, argues Anurag Gurtu, co-founder and CEO of Airrived. In this guest commentary he urges buyers and investors to examine deployment costs and gross margins to distinguish sustainable software businesses from expensive staffing operations.
title: The FDE Bubble: Silicon Valley’s Most Expensive Game Of Pretend

summary: As AI enables smaller, faster teams, companies should hire curious, adaptable people who challenge established practices and can be trusted to make independent decisions, according to guest author Eric Francia, who writes that giving employees real responsibility, encouraging questions and investing in continuous learning helps teams innovate, stay engaged and retain talent.
title: How To Build Your Team With Autonomous Humans, Not Just Autonomous Systems
